correctness.rationale: Independently differentiated the axial support function and recovered principal radii 1−2tz³ and 1+t(6z−8z³). Their global extrema bound convexity exactly by |t|≤1/2, including semidefinite endpoints. Great-circle restriction has first harmonic (translation) and third-harmonic coefficient t(1−(e·v)²)^(3/2)/4, yielding area through the planar support-function identity. For uniform V, e·V is uniform on [−1,1], giving Y=(1−Z²)^3 and the claimed CDF with t=0 correctly excluded. Independently integrated the 3D support curvature determinant for K and for brightness as support of ΠK, recovering both intrinsic-volume identities and the exact sextic projection-body volume. The derivative of its normalized sextic is strictly negative for 0<t≤1/2; the endpoint ratio follows by substitution. No finite direction sample is used as proof.

Those are explicitly prior coverage and confer no novelty credit. The surviving brightness profile, normalized random-area distribution, inverse amplitude identification and sharp projection-body volume are distinct natural invariants not covered by that theorem. The Myroshnychenko–Ryabogin–Saroglou primary paper discusses threefold-projection rigidity/existence, not these projection-body volume calculations in the materially read pages. Abas develops random brightness primarily for polytopes; complete 92-page text was not accessible. Best-of-knowledge originality passes only for the surviving invariants.
